[center][b][color=#ff7700]Pixel‑perfect farmer frame exporter and NPC generator. Outputs 16×32 PNGs for every vanilla farmer action and can generate fully‑dressed NPCs with Stardew‑style randomization or explicit outfit overrides. Outputs all animation frames, as well as a ready-to-use sheet with all movement included for basic NPCs.[/color][/b][/center]

[center][color=#ff7700][size=4][b]I[/b][/size][b]nstructions[/b][/color][/center]
[center]
[color=#ff7700]1) Download the latest version and extract it next to your Stardew Valley.exe.[/color][/center]
[center][color=#ff7700]2) Create an input/ folder next to FarmSplitter.exe containing the base farmer sprites you’ve extracted from your game (or your mod setup):[/color]


[code]accessories.png
farmer_base.png
farmer_base_bald.png
farmer_girl_base.png
farmer_girl_base_bald.png
hairstyles.png
hairstyles2.png
hats.png
pants.png
shirts.png
shoeColors.png
skinColors.png[/code][/center]
[center]
[color=#ff7700]
3) Run it. By default it exports per‑action frames into output/.[/color]

[color=#00ff00]./FarmSplitter.exe[/color]
[color=#ffff00][size=1](This will generate a single ranom NPC.)[/size][/color]


[color=#ff7700]4) Generate multiple NPCs with progress feedback:[/color]

[color=#00ff00]./FarmSplitter.exe --random 25[/color]

[color=#ff7700]Placing the tool next to Stardew Valley.exe ensures it can read the game’s Content data and SDL2.dll. If you want to run it elsewhere, copy the SDL2.dll next to FarmerSplitter.exe and use --content <path>.[/color]

[color=#ff7700][size=4][b]CLI Reference[/b][/size][/color]
[left]
[code]
Core
- -random <n>: generate n NPCs (shows a console progress bar)
- --gender <male|female|both>: source pool for random gender (default both)
- --male-only / --female-only: shorthand for --gender
- --seed <n>: deterministic generation
- --content <path> or --content-dir <path>: game Content root (default: ./Content)

[*]--actions <a,b,c>: export only actions whose names contain any of the comma‑separated filters (case‑insensitive substring)
[*]--verbose: log chosen outfit and color details per NPC, plus any per‑action export warnings


Hats & Accessories (disabled by default)
- --hats <yes|no>: enable/disable hats when not explicitly set
- --accessories <yes|no>: enable/disable accessories when not explicitly set
- --p-hat <0..1>: hat probability (applied if hats are enabled and no explicit --hat)
- --p-acc <0..1>: accessory probability (applied if accessories are enabled and no explicit --accessory)

Explicit Outfit Overrides (skip randomization for that piece)
- --shirt <id>: shirt ID from Data/Shirts
- --pants <id>: pants ID from Data/Pants
- --hair <index>: hair index (e.g., male 0–15/108–117, female 16–40)
- --hat <index>: hat ID (or -1 to force none)
- --accessory <index>: accessory index (or -1 to force none)
- --haircolor <RRGGBB>: exact hair color hex (e.g., 191919 or #191919)
- --pantscolor <RRGGBB>: exact pants color hex
- --shoeindex <row>: row in Characters/Farmer/shoeColors palette
- --shoecolor <RRGGBB>: target shoe color; the closest palette row is selected automatically

Gender Heuristics
- Hair range enforcement is on by default (male: 0–15 or 108–117; female: 16–40).
[*] --no-enforce-gender-hair disables this guard (useful for testing).
- Male shirt exclusions (same set as CharacterCustomization) are on by default.
[*] --no-strict-male-shirts disables the exclusions and allows all shirts for male.


Notes on randomization
- Hair ranges match CharacterCustomization (male: 0–15 or 108–117, female: 16–40).
- Male shirt pool excludes the same set as CharacterCustomization.
- Pants color and hair color use the same weighted adjustments and overrides as CharacterCustomization unless you pass explicit hex values.
- Shoes are randomized from the palette unless --shoeindex/--shoecolor are given.
- Pants ID 1 are shorts. The tool equips pants as a Clothing item (like the game), so shorts render consistently across frames. Random generation still avoids 1 by default; you can force them with --pants 1.

Output Layout

Exports go under output/:
- Body/, Arms/, Pants/, Shirts/Overlays/, Accessories/, Hats/, Hairstyles/ – per‑action, per‑frame PNGs at 16×32
- NPCs/NPC_0001/<Male|Female>/<Action>/frameX.png – composed frames for each generated NPC
- Each NPC directory includes a legend.json describing the chosen styles (shirt, pants, hair, hat, accessory) and gender.
- A movement spritesheet is created for every NPC at NPCs/NPC_0001/Sheet/movement.png (64×128):

[*]Row 1: walkDown frame0..frame3
[*]Row 2: walkRight frame0..frame3
[*]Row 3: walkUp frame0..frame3
[*]Row 4: walkLeft frame0..frame3
[*]Each frame is 16×32, tightly packed with no spacing for direct use in sprite‑based tools.[/code][/left]

[color=#ff7700][size=4][b]Examples[/b][/size]

Random 20 NPCs, hats + accessories enabled:[/color]

[color=#00ff00]./FarmSplitter.exe --random 20 --hats yes --accessories yes[/color]

[color=#ff7700]Only export walking actions and build movement sheets (quiet run):[/color]

[color=#00ff00]./FarmSplitter.exe --random 12 --actions WalkingDown,WalkingRight,WalkingUp,WalkingLeft[/color]


[color=#ff7700]Exact outfit with colors:[/color]

[color=#00ff00]./FarmSplitter.exe --gender male --shirt 1021 --pants 0 --hair 11 --haircolor 191919 --pantscolor 1e90ff --hat 4 --accessory 6 --shoecolor a0522d[/color]

[color=#ff7700]Run outside the game folder (point to Content):[/color]

[color=#00ff00]./FarmSplitter.exe --random 10 --content "C:\\Program Files (x86)\\Steam\\steamapps\\common\\Stardew Valley\\Content"[/color]



[size=4][b]Troubleshooting[/b][/size]
[color=#ff7700]- "Error: could not locate Stardew Valley Content": place the tool next to Stardew Valley.exe or pass --content <path> pointing at the game’s Content folder.[/color]
[color=#ff7700]- MonoGame/SDL init error: ensure SDL2.dll is next to the executable (the release zip includes it) and that Content is readable.[/color]
[color=#ff7700]- Per‑action export warnings: the exporter will continue and log the action name; rerun with --verbose for more detail.[/color]

[size=4][b]Tips[/b][/size]
[color=#ff7700]- Keep FarmSplitter.exe next to Stardew Valley.exe and place the listed input/*.png there for the smoothest experience.[/color]
[color=#ff7700]- Frames are pixel‑perfect 16×32 crops rendered by the vanilla `FarmerRenderer`, so layering and offsets match the game exactly.[/color]
